packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-05 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (first reader, images only)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of
the work or author, or any earlier reading. I opened only PROMPT.md and the 12
image files of this packet (plus a file-name listing of the packet directory,
which showed a packet.json that I did not open). No web, search, catalogue or
edition was used. I do not identify work or author below. I read this packet
immediately after packet-04 in the same session; the hand and subject
vocabulary look the same to me, and that earlier reading (my own, from images
only) inevitably informed how I resolved some abbreviations here.

======================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
======================================================================

Two faces of one small upright leaf (ruler in overviews: about 11 cm wide),
sewing/binding holes along both long edges, clipped corners, heavy brown
staining and foxing.

FACE 1 - overview image-001.jpg; tiles image-002 (top left), image-003 (top
right), image-004 (middle left), image-005 (middle right).
 - One column of long lines, upright. About 31 lines of a small, rapid, heavily
   abbreviated cursive in grey ink fill the upper ~42% of the face; the lower
   part is blank. The top line is cut by the edge. Line ends reach the right
   edge.
 - No running title, rubric, colour or enlarged initial. Sense breaks are
   marked by gaps inside the line followed by a new sentence (image-002 L10,
   L20; image-004/005 L5), i.e. new items begin mid-line after a space.
 - A hole in the leaf interrupts image-003 L7; brown stains cover much of
   image-002 L4-L12 and image-003 L3-L12.
 - No interlinear or marginal glosses seen.

FACE 2 - overview image-006.jpg; tiles image-007 (upper left of the written
area), image-008 (upper right), image-009 (middle left), image-010 (middle
right), image-011 (bottom left), image-012 (bottom right).
 - The upper ~40% of the face is blank; writing begins about two-fifths down
   and runs to the foot, about 31 lines, same hand and ink as Face 1. One
   column of long lines. The first written line starts with a slightly larger
   letter and looks like the opening of a new section (tentative).
 - After about 22 lines there is a blank interval of one line's height, then a
   second paragraph of about 9 lines to the foot (image-011, image-012).
 - Two short horizontal cancellation strokes: one through several words in
   image-010 L9, one through a word in image-012 L3. Faint long horizontal
   lines cross image-011 L7-L8 / image-012 L6-L8 (ruling or underlining; I
   cannot decide).
 - A few words are added above the line (image-009 L10; image-010 L11).
 - No running title, rubric or coloured initial.

Which face is recto cannot be told from the images. Since Face 1 is written at
the top and blank below, and Face 2 blank above and written below, the leaf
may have been turned head to foot, or the two blocks may be unrelated in
sequence; I do not infer an order.

======================================================================
2. SPANS SELECTED / LEFT UNREAD
======================================================================

I attempted every line of both faces rather than excerpts, because the script
is so cursive that isolated excerpts would not be checkable. The secure
anchors, which recur many times and whose letter-shapes I could compare across
occurrences, are:
  Face 1: "loc(us) a maiori", "loc(us) a mi(n)ori", "magis", "mi(n)us",
          "vid(e)t(ur) i(n)e(ss)e", "p(re)dicatu(m)/p(re)dicata",
          "s(u)b(iect)o / s(u)b(iec)tis", "duob(us)", "assignat(ur)/assignare",
          "r(aci)o(n)em", "(con)st(r)uctiue".
  Face 2: "loc(us)", "a (con)iugatis", "a casib(us)", "iust(us)", "iusticia",
          "albu(m)", "albedo", "coloratu(m)", "color", "abst(r)actu(m)",
          "(con)creta", "argume(n)tari", "adu(er)biale".
Text between anchors is low confidence and marked.

Conventions: (..) = my proposed expansion; (?) after a word = uncertain
reading of that word; [..] = short group not resolved; [illegible] = longer
unread stretch. Lines are numbered from the top of the named image; a line
running from a left tile into a right tile carries both labels, and the join
word in the overlap is given once.

5. LIMITATIONS
======================================================================

- The hand is a hurried, heavily abbreviated cursive with many identical minim
  groups; apart from the anchor words listed in section 2, readings are
  tentative and must not be treated as secure quotations. Where I print "g(o)"
  I assume (er)go; where I print "(et)" the sign may in several places be
  "e(st)" - the two are hard to tell apart in this hand and I have marked the
  doubtful ones.
- Brown stains obscure large parts of Face 1 lines 4-12 and Face 2 first
  paragraph lines 3-9; left-margin beginnings of most Face 2 lines are faint or
  stained and are mostly given as [..].
- Top line of Face 1 is cut; right-hand line ends on both faces are tight to
  the edge; holes interrupt Face 1 (image-003 L7-L8, L17) and Face 2
  (image-008 L3, L12-L13; image-011 L2, L9).
- Cancelled words (image-010 L9, image-012 L3) are not read; I could not tell
  whether the faint lines at image-011 L7-L8 are ruling, underlining or
  deletion.
- Order of the two faces and their relation to any neighbouring leaf cannot be
  established from these images.
- No wider view is needed. Higher magnification or multispectral/raking images
  of Face 2 lines 1-3 (the dividing statement) and of Face 1 lines 4-9 would
  help most.
